The Goal

Connect a line of 4 pieces (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) that share at least one common characteristic.

The Catch: You do not choose which piece you get to play! Your opponent picks the piece for you, and you must pick an unused piece to hand back to them.

 How to Play

The game is played on a 4×4 board with 16 unique pieces.

Every piece has 4 distinct traits:

  • Color: Light or Dark
  • Height: Tall or Short
  • Shape: Round or Square
  • Core: Solid or Hollow

Each Turn in 3 Easy Steps

  1. Check your piece: Look at the piece your opponent handed you.
  2. Place it: Put it on any empty square (row, col) on the board.
  3. Pass a piece: Choose any remaining piece from the pool and hand it to your opponent!

Note on Turn 1: Player 1 doesn't place a piece yet; they just pick an initial piece to give to Player 2.

Winning the Game

You win immediately if the piece you place completes any line of 4 (row, column, or diagonal) where all 4 pieces share any one trait:

  • All 4 are Tall (or all 4 are Short)
  • All 4 are Dark (or all 4 are Light)
  • All 4 are Square (or all 4 are Round)
  • All 4 are Hollow (or all 4 are Solid)

If all 16 squares are filled without a winning line, the game is a Draw.

 Input / Output Protocol

What Your Bot Receives Each Turn

Line 1: pieceToPlace — The piece ID (0 to 15) you must place on the board (or -1 on the very first turn).

Lines 2–5: 4 lines representing the 4×4 grid. Each row contains 4 numbers separated by spaces: -1 if the square is empty, or the piece ID (0–15).

Line 6: availableCount — How many pieces are left in the pool.

Line 7: Space-separated list of available piece IDs you can give to your opponent.

What Your Bot Must Print (Stdout)

Print a single line containing:

<row> <col> <pieceToGive> [optional_message]
  • Standard Turn: 1 2 7 Good luck! — Places received piece at row 1, col 2, and hands piece 7 to your opponent.
  • First Turn (Player 1): -1 -1 7 — No piece to place, simply hands piece 7 to Player 2.
  • Final Turn (16th piece): 3 3 -1 — Places the last piece; no pieces left to give.
Pro-Tip: Piece IDs & Bitmasks

Every piece ID (0 to 15) is just a 4-bit integer:

Bit 0: Color (0 = Light, 1 = Dark) | Bit 1: Height (0 = Short, 1 = Tall)
Bit 2: Shape (0 = Round, 1 = Square) | Bit 3: Core (0 = Solid, 1 = Hollow)

To test if 4 pieces a, b, c, d share an attribute:

boolean isQuarto = ((a & b & c & d) | ((~a & ~b & ~c & ~d) & 0x0F)) != 0;
